protocol.calibration: regular pilots; same original HEVC iteration count in every refactor case
protocol.case_order: seeded shuffle per complete A/B/C block
protocol.bootstrap: 10000 paired resamples; median ratio and recomputed p95 ratio
protocol.gil_off: default only; no PYTHON_GIL=0 or -X gil=0; check after imports/warmup/work
protocol.adaptive: pilot duration and skip blocked modes/cases; fixed balanced repetition count, no repeat-until-pass
protocol.cold_pool: pool create and shutdown included in every evaluate call
protocol.hot_pool: one pool per child; initialized by warmup, reused across measured evaluations
protocol.snapshot_compute: snapshot creation + cold evaluation; excludes ORM/SQL/network
protocol.rss: child lifetime high-water includes imports/setup and may include fork/exec floor

limitations: The normalized Python psycopg/libpq backend is not parity with production psycopg-binary.
Pure HEVC compute scaling is not end-to-end ALTT/API/worker acceleration.
No Session/ORM object crosses a worker boundary; DB and external I/O are excluded.
Hot pools and prebuilt snapshots are upper-bound compute scenarios, not current production behavior.
BLAKE3 single-threaded local cached-file I/O is not Unraid array throughput or encoder speed.
Small-sample p95 intervals may be inconclusive; no zero-slowdown claim from median alone.
Native arm64 Linux results cannot establish target Unraid amd64 performance.
